exam.title: MIT 6.0001: Object-Oriented Programming & Big-O Complexity
exam.description: Higher education exam covering class hierarchies, encapsulation, inheritance, asymptotic Big-O analysis, and merge sort.
exam.instructions: Answer all questions rigorously showing all work where applicable. Time limit: 60 minutes.

questions.text: What is the worst-case asymptotic time complexity of Merge Sort on a list of n elements?
questions.rubric: Merge Sort recursively splits the list into halves (log n levels of recursion) and takes O(n) time to merge at each level, giving O(n log n) in all cases (best, average, worst).

questions.text: In a Python class definition, what is the role of the special method `__str__(self)`?
options: It converts any input string into an integer.
It returns an informal, readable string representation of the object when passed to print() or str().
It destructs the string from memory upon garbage collection.
It hashes the string for dictionary insertion.
questions.correct_answer: It returns an informal, readable string representation of the object when passed to print() or str().
questions.rubric: __str__ defines human-readable string representation of instances when str() or print() is called.

questions.text: Explain why Binary Search requires an already sorted array to guarantee O(log n) time complexity, and compare its performance against Linear Search on an unsorted list of 1,000,000 items.
questions.correct_answer: Binary search relies on order to discard half the elements per step (log2(10^6) ~ 20 checks vs 1,000,000 checks in linear search).
questions.rubric: Full marks for explaining that order allows decision on which half contains the target; noting that log2(1,000,000) is approximately 20 comparisons compared to up to 1,000,000 in linear search.
